answer: A claimant lowers a crystal anchor onto a named tide-gauge chain and fixes a mirror to its shank, so at dawn the mirror throws a light spot onto a crystal marker stone on the quay. Two harbor wardens measure the spot against the tide register within three days, checking the anchor weight against the foundry log and the mirror polish against the glazier ledger. A missing anchor, a spot off the mark, or a gauge claimed twice voids the season, burns a 280-credit stake, and bars the harbor two seasons; 1,000 fakes mean 1,000 crystal anchors lowered and 1,000 mirrors polished by hand at dawn.
